pages.title: API Performance Observatory — Project Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the project: what it does, its two-tier architecture (Go backend + React frontend), key capabilities, and how to navigate the wiki. Links to child pages for setup and architecture details.

pages.title: Getting Started & Configuration
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for setting up the project locally: environment variables, database connection, frontend build tooling, and running both services. Covers backend .env configuration (DB_HOST, JWT_SECRET, etc.) and frontend VITE_API_BASE_URL.

pages.title: Technology Stack
pages.purpose: Detailed breakdown of all major dependencies: Go/Gin/GORM on the backend; React 19/Vite/TanStack Query/Zustand/Recharts/Tailwind CSS on the frontend. Explains why each library was chosen and how they interact.

pages.title: Backend Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the Go backend's layered architecture: cmd entrypoint → routes → handlers → services → repositories → models. Introduces the dependency injection pattern and links to child pages for each layer.

pages.title: Server Entrypoint & Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Deep dive into main.go: initialization sequence, dependency wiring, concurrent execution of the HTTP server and scheduler goroutine, graceful shutdown with SIGINT/SIGTERM handling, and the 10-second shutdown timeout.

pages.title: HTTP Routing & Middleware
pages.purpose: Documents the Gin router setup in routes.go: all route groups (/auth, /endpoints, /healthchecks, /incidents, /dashboard), CORS configuration, and the JWT AuthMiddleware that protects all non-auth routes.

pages.title: Data Models & Database
pages.purpose: Covers the five GORM models (User, Endpoint, HealthCheck, Incident, Monitoring), their fields and relationships, the PostgreSQL connection setup in postgres.go, AutoMigrate behavior, and the DSN selection logic (DatabaseURL vs individual fields).

pages.title: Repository Layer
pages.purpose: Explains the repository pattern: interfaces vs concrete implementations for EndpointRepository, HealthCheckRepository, IncidentRepository, MonitoringRepository, and UserRepository. Covers GORM query patterns, pagination with offset/limit, and context propagation.

pages.title: Service Layer
pages.purpose: Overview of all twelve service files and how they encapsulate business logic. Introduces the service dependency graph (HealthCheckService → IncidentService, DashboardService → all repos) and links to child pages for each major service.

pages.title: Health Check & Scheduler Services
pages.purpose: Details the HealthCheckService.CheckEndpoint flow: HTTP GET with 3-retry logic, 10-second timeout, response time measurement, success/failure determination, and automatic incident creation/resolution. Also covers SchedulerService: the per-minute ticker, ShouldCheck logic using CheckInterval, and the semaphore-limited goroutine pool (max 10 concurrent checks).

pages.title: Incident Service & Statistics
pages.purpose: Documents the IncidentService lifecycle: StartIncident, ResolveIncident, GetActiveIncidentByEndpointID, and paginated retrieval. Covers IncidentStatsService for uptime/downtime calculations, UptimeReportService, PerformanceStatsService, SuccessRateService, and HistoricalReportService.

pages.title: Dashboard Service & Aggregation
pages.purpose: Explains how DashboardService aggregates data from all four repositories into dashboard DTOs: GetOverview (healthy/unhealthy counts), GetStatus/GetStatusPaginated, GetRecentIncidents (in-memory join), GetPerformance, GetSuccessRate, GetUptime, GetHistory (30-day), and GetMonitoring. Highlights the iterative N+1 lookup pattern and delegation to specialized stateless services.

pages.title: Handlers & DTOs
pages.purpose: Covers the seven handler files (auth, endpoint, health_check, incident, dashboard, monitoring, stats) and the twelve DTO files. Explains how handlers parse requests, call services, and use the utils/response.go helpers (OK, Created, PaginatedOK, etc.) to return standardized JSON responses.

pages.title: Authentication & Security
pages.purpose: Documents the full auth flow: registration (bcrypt password hashing), login (JWT generation with 24-hour expiry, HS256 signing), cookie-based token delivery, AuthMiddleware validation, and the apperrors sentinel values (ErrUserAlreadyExists, ErrInvalidCredentials). Covers the Claims struct and UserID injection into Gin context.

pages.title: Frontend Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the React SPA: Vite build system, routing structure (ProtectedRoute/PublicRoute), layout hierarchy (MainLayout + TopNav + AuthLayout), and the data-fetching strategy using TanStack Query hooks. Links to child pages for each major area.

pages.title: Routing, Layouts & Navigation
pages.purpose: Explains the React Router setup: createBrowserRouter with ProtectedRoute/PublicRoute guards, the MainLayout wrapper, TopNav component (desktop + mobile responsive nav, active link styling, logout flow), and AuthLayout for login/register pages. Covers the Zustand authStore integration for route protection.

pages.title: State Management & API Client
pages.purpose: Documents the Zustand authStore (user, isAuthenticated, isCheckingAuth, persist middleware with 'apo-auth' key), the Axios apiClient (baseURL from VITE_API_BASE_URL, withCredentials, 401 auto-logout interceptor), and the AuthInit component for session restoration on page load.

pages.title: API Layer & React Query Hooks
pages.purpose: Covers all six API modules (auth.ts, client.ts, endpoints.ts, dashboard.ts, healthchecks.ts, incidents.ts) and the four hook files (useDashboard.ts, useEndpoints.ts, useHealthChecks.ts, useIncidents.ts). Explains how TanStack Query wraps Axios calls, manages caching, and exposes isLoading/isError/refetch to page components.

pages.title: UI Component Library
pages.purpose: Documents the shared component library under frontend/src/components/ui: Badge, Box, Button, Card, EmptyState, ErrorState, Input, MiniStatisticsCard, Modal, Pagination, Select, Skeleton/TableSkeleton, Table, and Typography. Explains the NOC console design language, Tailwind CSS utility patterns, and the cn() utility for conditional class merging.

pages.title: Frontend Pages & Features
pages.purpose: Overview of all eight page components and the features directory. Explains the common patterns: URL-based pagination state, dual-query strategies, client-side data processing, and ErrorState retry callbacks. Links to child pages for each major page.

pages.title: Dashboard Page & Widgets
pages.purpose: Deep dive into DashboardPage: the seven data hooks it orchestrates, client-side ranking logic for Top Slowest/Top Error Rate endpoints, CSS Grid layout (left stats, center globe, right rankings, bottom logs). Documents all DashboardWidgets: EndpointStatusList, IncidentTimeline, HealthCheckList, RankedEndpoints, and the MonitoringGlobe 3D visualization with COBE library and mock arc data.

pages.title: Endpoint Management & Details Pages
pages.purpose: Covers EndpointsPage (CRUD operations, server-side pagination/search/status filtering, create/edit modal sharing, useSearchParams for page state) and EndpointDetailsPage (per-endpoint telemetry: stats, monitoring info, 24-hour response time chart with 4-hour bucket aggregation, health check log, incident timeline). Documents ChartCard with Recharts area/bar chart modes.

pages.title: Health Checks & Incidents Pages
pages.purpose: Documents HealthChecksPage (endpoint + success filters, URL-based pagination, status_code=0 normalized to 404) and IncidentsPage (dual-query strategy for active + historical incidents, duration calculation fallback, severity badge coloring, Link navigation to endpoint details). Covers the format.ts utility functions used across both pages.

pages.title: Authentication Pages & Profile
pages.purpose: Covers LoginPage (email/password form, JWT cookie receipt, authStore update), RegisterPage (new account creation), and ProfilePage (GET /auth/me, authStore sync, JWT Bearer token display). Explains the PublicRoute guard that redirects authenticated users away from login/register.

pages.title: Monitoring Engine
pages.purpose: Explains the end-to-end automated monitoring pipeline: how the scheduler triggers health checks, how results flow into incidents, and how the stats layer computes derived metrics. This is the core value-add of the observatory.

pages.title: Scheduler & Check Execution
pages.purpose: Details the SchedulerService tick loop (1-minute interval), ShouldCheck logic (LastCheckedAt + CheckInterval), concurrent goroutine dispatch with a semaphore of 10, LastCheckedAt update after each check, and context cancellation for graceful shutdown.

pages.title: Incident Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Documents the full incident state machine: detection (CheckEndpoint failure → GetActiveIncidentByEndpointID → StartIncident if none exists), persistence (IncidentRepository.Create), resolution (endpoint recovery → ResolveIncident sets ResolvedAt + IsResolved=true), and reporting (GetIncidentsPaginated with isResolvedStr filter).

pages.title: Performance & Uptime Statistics
pages.purpose: Covers the stateless analytics services: PerformanceStatsService (min/max/average response time), SuccessRateService (success/failure ratios), IncidentStatsService (total downtime minutes, uptime percentage), UptimeReportService, HistoricalReportService (30-day period combining performance + success), and the legacy stats.CalculateStats function.

pages.title: API Reference
pages.purpose: Complete reference for all REST endpoints exposed by the backend, organized by resource group. Covers request/response shapes, authentication requirements, pagination parameters, and links to the Swagger/OpenAPI documentation.

pages.title: Auth & Endpoint Routes
pages.purpose: Documents /auth (POST /register, POST /login, POST /logout, GET /me) and /endpoints (CRUD + /stats, /incidents, /monitoring sub-routes). Includes request body schemas from DTOs, response formats, and authentication requirements.
